title: I Wept for Youth with Tears in My Eyes
intro: Shukri Faisal prints these four verses in his edition of Abu al-Atahiya in the order Omar al-Sharafi recites them. At first the speaker sounds like a mourner at a death. Grey hair brings him the news of his loss, and a bare branch gives it a shape. He ends by imagining himself telling the whole story to the youth he has lost.

translation: I wept for youth, tears in my eyes,
but neither tears nor sobs did any good.
1.sharh: The tears can be seen and the sobs heard. Neither brings back the youth he mourns.

translation: How bitterly I grieved for a youth
whose death grey hair and a dyed head announced.
2.sharh: Even the dye he uses to cover his grey hair gives his age away. Both the grey and its disguise bring the same news.

translation: I was stripped of youth while it was fresh,
as a branch is stripped of its leaves.
3.sharh: The man is still there, as the bare branch is. The word for the freshness he has lost belongs equally to a young body and a green shoot.

translation: If only youth would come back one day,
so I could tell it what old age has done.
4.sharh: If youth could come back, the first thing he would do is confide in it. The companion he mourns is the one to whom he longs to tell the story.

1.2.2.head: أَغنى
1.2.2.meaning: To avail, to do some good.

1.2.5.head: النَّحيب
1.2.5.meaning: Weeping that can be heard, sobbing aloud.

2.2.1.head: نَعى
2.2.1.meaning: To announce a death. Here grey hair brings the news.

2.2.4.head: الخَضيب
2.2.4.meaning: Dyed, said here of hair coloured to cover the grey.

3.1.5.head: غَضّ
3.1.5.meaning: Tender and fresh, like new growth.
